The most underrated GTM move right now? Running ChatGPT, Claude Code, and Clay in the same pipeline. I ran all three side by side this quarter for client campaigns and honestly the difference isn't which one is "best" - it's how they each do something the others can't. ChatGPT's custom GPTs let me turn my best processes into repeatable SOPs. ICP research, competitor analysis, email drafts - all templatized so the output stays consistent even when I'm running ten campaigns at once. If you're doing the same type of research over and over, you should be building a GPT for it. Claude Code lets me build, test, and iterate on outbound scripts, data processing pipelines, and automation logic right from my terminal. No separate dev setup, no context switching. If you've ever wanted to just describe what you need and have it built in front of you, that's what this feels like. Clay runs the enrichment and scoring engine underneath everything. Set up your table once with waterfall enrichment across multiple providers, build your scoring logic, and it pushes qualified leads into your outbound tool of choice through native integrations. Once it's configured you barely have to look at it. The wins don't come from any single tool getting better. They come from how the three connect. Clay surfaces the signal and enriches the lead on autopilot. Claude Code turns that enriched data into custom scripts that generate messaging like you spent 20 minutes researching each prospect. ChatGPT fills the gaps in between - quick research, rapid iteration, the stuff that used to eat your whole morning. Picking one is like choosing between an engine, steering wheel, and fuel. You need all three to actually move. Stacking is the game now. → Clay runs your data engine → Claude Code builds your outbound logic → ChatGPT keeps you fast The best GTM teams aren't picking favorites - they're building systems. Which AI are you leaning on the most for outbound right now, and what's the gap you're still trying to fill?

Most sales teams track emails sent and calls made. I track pipeline per rep. This might seem like a small difference. But it's not: These are completely different ways of measuring success. (i… | S. Can Timağur
Most sales teams track emails sent and calls made. I track pipeline per rep. This might seem like a small difference. But it's not: These are completely different ways of measuring success. (i know, metrics aren't sexy. but just bare with me) Because traditional metrics show activity. Flywheel metrics show momentum. Old school metrics tell you: - How many impressions you got - How many emails went out - How many calls happened My metrics tell me way more: 1. Pipeline per rep: Is each person actually creating quality opportunities? 2. Win rate by strategic fit: Are we talking to the right buyers or wasting time? 3. Time to opportunity: How fast are new accounts actually engaging with us? 4. Multi-threading depth: Are we reaching the full buying group or just one person? 5. Revenue velocity: How quickly are deals moving from first touch to close? These aren't just performance indicators. They're momentum indicators. Traditional metrics make you feel busy: - Active - Productive - Working hard But my metrics show you what's actually working. They show if you're building real pipeline or just checking boxes. I tell my clients all the time to shift their focus. Because activity doesn't equal results. Momentum does. If you're still measuring success by emails sent and calls made, you're missing the bigger picture. Which is fine if you just want to stay busy. But if you want to scale revenue: Track momentum, not just activity. Measure what moves deals forward. Focus on velocity. Trust me on this.

Growth, RevOps, GTM Engineer, Sales Ops, WTF guys? Everyone uses these titles. Nobody agrees on what they mean. Here&#39;s the simplest way to think about it: → Growth decides what to do and where to… | Mat To Market
Growth, RevOps, GTM Engineer, Sales Ops, WTF guys? Everyone uses these titles. Nobody agrees on what they mean. Here's the simplest way to think about it: → Growth decides what to do and where to grow. → RevOps owns the entire revenue journey, from product to cash. → Sales Ops keeps the sales team running smoothly. → GTM Engineer builds the technical workflows that make it all work. Now let's break each one down Sales Ops → Makes the sales team run like clockwork. CRM, forecasting, territories, comp plans. If a rep has friction before booking a meeting, Sales Ops removes it. RevOps → Covers the entire revenue journey. From product catalog to quote to cash collection. It aligns Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Finance under one umbrella. Where Sales Ops optimizes one team, RevOps connects every team that touches revenue. The goal: one data model, one process, zero silos. Growth → Finds the fastest path to revenue. SEO, paid, content, product loops, conversion — whatever moves the needle. The mindset is: test fast, double down on what works, kill what doesn't. GTM Engineer → The newest role, and the most technical. Builds the workflows that make everyone else 10x faster. Enrichment waterfalls, Clay tables, API integrations, AI sequences. If Growth decides what to do, the GTM Engineer builds how it actually runs. At early-stage: one person wears all four hats. At scale: they're four teams that need to talk to each other every single day. The best setups I've seen? A clear owner for each layer. The worst? Everyone's doing everything and nothing actually ships. Are you agree? What’s your definition?

Only ICP-fit accounts move forward Step 2: Detect buying signals ↳ Hiring surges, funding rounds, G2 reviews, tech stack changes ↳ Tools: Apify, Clay, PredictLeads, Lonescale, FactorsAI, Vector CommonRoom all connected via MCP Step 3: Find decision-makers ↳ Apollo /Clay pulls contacts from HubSpot , Clay enriches, and routes them ↳ Champion, Economic Buyer, Influencer, Blocker (mapped automatically) Step 4: Enrich across 3-8 providers ↳ Waterfalling runs in the background: verified email + phone before anyone touches the account through Clay Step 5: Generate personalised copy ↳ Claude infers your value proposition, differentiation, and what is currently converting Step 6: Push to campaign ↳ Instantly.ai , Smartlead, EmailBison, Heyreach, lemlist ↳ The right tool for the right tier is automatically routed Best of all? Step 7: Analyse what converts and feed this back to your sequencer ↳ Call transcripts ↳ Best-performing angles ↳ Flow back into the skills automatically, so your system gets smarter and better over time. (without rebuilding anything from scratch or training anything again and again) The architecture is simple: You = Captain. You define the ICP, set the routing rules, and approve the plays.
